item.title: Gioele La Manno
item.description:
Bio

I earned my PhD at Karolinska Instituet and I am proud alumnus of the Linnarsson Lab. My original training is in Biotechnology (BSc @UNIPA) and Biomedicine (MSc @KI) but nowadays I will probably turn around if somebody is calling out for a Molecular Biologist, Computational Biologist or Bioinformatician.

My research focuses on understanding brain development. I am particularly interested in describing the sequence of states that embryonic stem cells go through during their differentiation towards mature neurons.

I have been tackling this question using machine learning tools on the wealth of data provided by single cell RNA sequencing, a technique I have been working with and developing since its early times.

My long-term goal is to contribute in making biology from a descriptive to a predictive science.

View the awards history, including the Eppendorf & Science Prize, FENS Research Award, and annual Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher recognition.

The EPFL inaugural lecture biography also describes the earlier Vasco Sanz, EMPIRIS, SIB, and Chorafas awards.

item.title: Congratulations, PI Toni! A new lab in Granada
item.description:
Congratulations to Antonio Herrera Camacho on becoming a Principal Investigator at the University of Granada! Supported by a Ramón y Cajal fellowship, Toni is starting his own independent research group. We are proud to celebrate this milestone with him.

Since joining the La Manno Lab in 2021, Toni has brought his experience in developmental biology to our efforts to understand how the brain forms. His work combined embryo culture, spatial transcriptomics, and single-cell analysis, with a particular interest in how folate deficiency affects brain development. Alongside his research, he helped students learn experimental approaches and develop their own projects.

His contributions also span several of the lab’s collaborative publications, including uMAIA, Spotiflow, and VeloCycle, all published in Nature Methods.

Seeing a colleague take the step to leading an independent lab is a special moment for our team. We look forward to the questions Toni and his new group will explore, and to continuing our scientific collaborations.

Thank you, Toni, for five years of science, mentorship, and friendship. We will miss having you in the lab, but there is much to celebrate. All the best for your new lab in Granada, PI Toni!

item.title: Gioele wins the Eppendorf & Science Prize for Neurobiology
item.description:
We are delighted to celebrate Gioele La Manno’s 2026 Eppendorf & Science Prize for Neurobiology.

The prize recognises research on brain lipid diversity, including the Lipid Brain Atlas. This milestone reflects a sustained collaboration across the lab and with Giovanni D’Angelo’s group.

Read Gioele’s accompanying essay, “Fats that think?”, in Science, and the official Eppendorf announcement.

Thank you to the students, researchers, and collaborators whose work made this possible.

item.title: Thank you and farewell, Francesco!
item.description:
We say goodbye to Francesco Danese and thank him for his time in the La Manno Lab.

Francesco joined us in August 2025 from Sapienza University of Rome for his master’s thesis.

Working with Luca Fusar Bassini, Francesco contributed to our neuroscience knowledge graph project, helping turn information from the scientific literature into structured knowledge that can support biological research. His work brought together machine learning, data science, and the practical challenges of processing a large collection of scientific papers.

Thank you, Francesco, for your contribution and collaboration. We wish you all the best for what comes next and look forward to staying in touch!

item.title: Thank you and farewell, Lothar!
item.description:
We say goodbye to Lothar Bezzon, who joined the lab in November 2025 for his master’s thesis research.

Working with Gioele La Manno and Luca Fusar Bassini, Lothar explored computational approaches to spatial lipidomics, including the use of independent datasets to benchmark models and test their predictions.

Thank you, Lothar, for your contribution to the lab. It was a pleasure to share this stage of your research with you, and we wish you all the best for your next steps!
